comments.author: @BruceWayne15325
comments.text:
As a coder for over 35yrs, I wouldn't say that AI won't affect our jobs. It already has. It's made those that use it much more effective. I simply don't believe that AI will be able to completely replace a coder until the AI companies change their approach. Until then, there will always be a need for someone telling the AI what to do, iterating over the design, etc.
We are already seeing some really stupid CEO's laying off their employees because they see that they can do the same amount of work with 30% or so less employees. The reason this is an idiotic business decision is that we live in a capitalist society. The companies that chase the short-term gains are going to open the door for their competition to come in and fly by them by continuing to hire the same number of employees and doing 30% more than before.
We will see stupid industry leaders trying to play catchup as they lose their vaunted lead, which is going to make their shareholders jump ship onto the smarter companies that didn't lay off their employees.

comments.author: @bigcauc7530
comments.text: What are your thoughts on making these different models cooperate like agents do? I was having them compete to answer some complex math questions and whenever i was unsure if one model was accurate, i offered the results to another model to verify and did that back and forth to make sure they would check each other and confirm one or the other. It seems to be the best way. Using one model, it gets lost in its own misinterpretations and doesn't know how to correct itself but if it's being checked by another model, they can work out kinks together and it makes a huge difference. I could see a game being made in a relatively similar time frame to studios by one person who knew how to get these models to get these models to work together properly and check each other.
